=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/claude_issue_route.py:1254-1279 | severity=blocker | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: `_cmd_security_dependency` validates issue identity before checking whether the issue has a security dependency, so incomplete metadata on an ordinary issue produces a false `held` verdict.
  WHY: The false hold can enter the clarify label-write path and fail the contract test; reviewers also note it can block ordinary issues with incomplete metadata.
- scripts/claude_issue_route.py:153-155 and 207-228 | severity=blocker | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The broad `Depends on:` line match treats ordinary prose as a dependency declaration and can hold issues that are not valid security follow-ups.
  WHY: The highest reported severity is BLOCKER; other reviewers rate the issue MAJOR. Ordinary issue text or legitimate security-finding prose containing `Depends on:` can be rejected or held instead of proceeding.
- .github/workflows/clarify.yml: lines 493-515 | severity=blocker | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The held-dependency branch changes `ISSUE_IMPLEMENTER` to `codex` and skips Codex before the Claude handoff, preventing Claude-routed follow-ups from reaching Claude intake and pickup.
  WHY: This conflicts with the stated requirement that Claude intake and pickup hold the follow-up; z-ai_glm-5_2 rated this MAJOR, while the other reviewers rated it BLOCKER.
- scripts/security_audit.sh: lines 1748-1752 and lines 1802-1823 | severity=blocker | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: An existing finding with no valid issue number is indexed with `0` and body path `-`, allowing the loop to pass `-` to `gh issue create --body-file -`.
  WHY: `gh` reads standard input as the issue body, consuming the index file and potentially creating a corrupted issue that prevents subsequent follow-ups from being processed; z-ai_glm-5_2 rated this MAJOR.
- scripts/claude_issue_route.py: lines 250-265 | severity=major | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: `fetch_security_dependency` calls `subprocess.run` without a timeout.
  WHY: A hung `gh api` call can block the queue, watchdog, or poller indefinitely.
- scripts/claude_issue_route.py: lines 1120-1135 | severity=major | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: `queue_stale` skips held dependencies, including missing or unresolvable prerequisites, without raising a stale alert.
  WHY: The dependent item can remain stuck in the queue silently; minimax_minimax-m3 reports a different behavior for this path and is listed separately below.
- scripts/claude_issue_route.py: lines 1791-1838 (the follow-up creation block; replaces the previous `gh_retry gh issue create ... >/dev/null` at line 1793 with `gh issue create ...` plus URL parsing) | severity=major | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Removing `gh_retry` from follow-up issue creation means a transient GitHub failure aborts the creation loop.
  WHY: Remaining follow-ups are not created until a later audit run.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh: lines 15836-15890 | severity=major | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The dependency-release block reads `comments_json` and `_standalone_staged_support_cache_available` before their per-iteration initialization, so later candidates can use the preceding issue's comments and cache state.
  WHY: Release-marker checks can post duplicate `/reclarify` comments or incorrectly skip release; the first iteration can also make redundant comment reads.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh: lines 15874-15876 | severity=major | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The release-marker check requires `"/reclarify\n"` and does not match a comment beginning with `"/reclarify\r\n"`.
  WHY: CRLF line endings can make the poller post duplicate `/reclarify` comments on each cycle.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh: lines 15873-15877 | severity=major | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The poller posts `/reclarify` for a ready dependency without checking whether the issue has advanced beyond `ai:clarification`.
  WHY: Clarification can be re-triggered for an issue already in a later phase, potentially moving it back and losing progress.
- scripts/claude_issue_route.py: lines 230-244; call sites in `queue_pending` (lines 891-900) and `queue_stale` (lines 1120-1140) | severity=blocker | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: When a prerequisite cannot be fetched, the queue treats the dependent item as held and ignored, while the watchdog may report a misleading `pickup_stalled` reason.
  WHY: A missing read or inaccessible private consumer repository can leave the item undispatched without a useful explanation.
- scripts/claude_issue_route.py: `queue_stale` (lines 1120-1140) | severity=major | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: A `ValueError` while validating a malformed prerequisite payload can be swallowed, suppressing the stale alert.
  WHY: A malformed dependency can leave the item stuck without a watchdog signal.
- .github/workflows/clarify.yml: lines 493-515 | severity=blocker | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The raw workflow `run:` block contains `${{ github.repository }}`, which the contract test executes without GitHub expression rendering.
  WHY: Bash receives the unrendered expression and fails; minimax_minimax-m3 also reports the same pattern in `.github/workflows/implement.yml` lines 1731, 1741, 2013, and 2018.
- .github/workflows/implement.yml: lines 1731, 1741, 2013, and 2018 | severity=major | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The workflow passes `${{ github.repository }}` directly in inline shell code rather than through an environment variable.
  WHY: The contract test's raw `run:` execution can reach Bash with the expression unrendered.
- changelog.d/4934-chain-security-followups.md: lines 1-2 | severity=nit | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The changelog fragment omits the required 3–5 sentence lead paragraph and audience-closing section.
  WHY: The fragment does not follow the structure required by CLAUDE.md section 20.D.
- scripts/security_audit.sh: line 1746 | severity=major | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The file path is hashed without normalization before same-file follow-ups are grouped.
  WHY: Equivalent path representations can produce different keys and bypass the intended same-file chaining.
- scripts/security_audit.sh: lines 1823-1826 | severity=major | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The follow-up URL prefix comparison is case-sensitive.
  WHY: A repository casing difference can reject a valid GitHub URL and abort the audit.
- scripts/security_audit.sh: lines 1817-1828 in the diff | severity=major | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: `LAST_FOLLOWUP_BY_FILE` is updated before the returned issue URL is verified.
  WHY: A failed creation that prints a URL can leave a dependency pointer to an issue that was not successfully created.
- scripts/security_audit.sh: lines 1743-1752 and 1802-1811 in the PR diff | severity=major | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The loop only learns an existing follow-up number when it reaches that finding in the current findings order.
  WHY: A new same-file finding that appears before an existing one can be created without a dependency and dispatched concurrently with it.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh: lines 15848-15856 | severity=major | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The standalone poller starts a separate dependency-check subprocess per candidate and does not cache reads for shared prerequisites.
  WHY: Candidates sharing a prerequisite cause redundant REST reads during a poller tick; z-ai_glm-5_2 rated this NIT.
- scripts/claude_issue_route.py: `SECURITY_DEPENDENCY_LINE_RE` definition (lines 153-155); `security_dependency_number` (lines 207-228) | severity=major | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: In a security finding, legitimate recommendation prose beginning with `Depends on:` can be treated as a malformed dependency declaration.
  WHY: The issue can be held indefinitely despite not containing a valid dependency reference.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh: lines 15873-15888 | severity=major | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The dependency-release path can move an issue that has reached a later phase back to `ai:clarification`.
  WHY: `/reclarify` triggers the clarification-label step without checking the issue's current phase.
- scripts/security_audit.sh: lines 1791-1838 | severity=major | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: A case-sensitive repository URL prefix check can reject a valid follow-up URL and terminate the audit.
  WHY: GitHub URL casing may differ from `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`.
- scripts/claude_issue_route.py: lines 423-466 and lines 396-406 | severity=nit | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: Cross-repository prerequisites are held without a recovery path in the helper.
  WHY: The reviewer describes this as a feature limitation rather than a contract break.
- .github/workflows/clarify.yml: diff lines 496-514 | severity=major | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The held-dependency branch applies `ai:clarification`, overrides the implementer, and can release an existing Claude claim before downstream gates finish.
  WHY: A Claude-routed follow-up has inconsistent claim and implementer state during the hold.
- scripts/claude_issue_route.py: `fetch_security_dependency` (diff lines 249-265), call sites in `claude_issue_intake.sh` (lines 240-256), `claude_issue_queue_watchdog.sh` (line 70), and `orchestrate_poll_process.sh` (line 15861) | severity=blocker | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: Dependency reads use a consumer repository from the queue payload, while the watchdog may lack access to a private consumer repository and does not apply the intake's allowed-repository check.
  WHY: A failed cross-repository read can leave dependent items stuck without surfacing the access failure to an operator.
